Short title extent and commencement

THE RECIPROCITY ACT, 1943
THE RECIPROCITY
ACT, 1943
ACT No. IX or 1943
(For Statement of Objects and Reasons, see Gazette of India,
1941, Pt. V, p. 162; and for Report of Select Committee, see ibid., 1943, Pt.
V, p. 57.
The Act has been applied to Baluchistan, see Notification No.
126‑F, dated the 18th August, 1943, Gazette of India, 1943, Pt. 1, p.
916.
It has been extended to‑
(a) the Leased Areas of Baluchistan by the Leased Areas
(Laws) Order, 1950 (G. G. O. 3 of 1950);
(b) the Baluchistan
States Union by the Baluchistan States Union (Federal Laws) (Extension) Order,
1953 (G. G. O. 4 of 1953), as amended;
(c) the Khairpur State, see the Khairpur (Federal Laws)
(Extension) Order, 1953 (G. G. O. 5 of 1953), as amended; and
(d) the State of Bahawalpur, see the Bahawalpur (Extension of
Federal Laws) Order, 1953 (G. G. O. 11 of 1953), as amended.
The Act has been and shall be deemed to have been brought
into force in Gwadur with effect from the 8th September, 1958, by the Gwadur
(Appli cation of Central Laws) Ordinance, 1960 (37 of 1960), s. 2.)
[31st March,
1943]
An Act to make
provisions on a basis of reciprocity in regard to
entry into,
travel, residence, the acquisition, holding or disposal
of property, the
enjoyment of educational facilities, the holding
of public office, or
the carrying on of any occupation, trade, business or profession in (Subs. by the Central Laws (Statute Reform) Ordinance, 1960
(21 of 1960), s. 3 and 2nd Sch. (with effect from the 14th October, 1955), for
"the provinces and the Capital of the Federation" which had been
subs. by A. O., 1949, for "British India".) [Pakistan] by,
and the franchise in (Subs. by the Central Laws
(Statute Reform) Ordinance, 1960 (21 of 1960), s. 3 and 2nd Sch. (with effect
from the 14th October, 1955), for "the provinces and the Capital of the
Federation" which had been subs. by A. O., 1949, for "British
India".)[Pakistan] of, persons domiciled in British Possessions.
WHEREAS it is expedient to make
provisions on a basis of reciprocity in regard to entry into, travel, residence,
the acquisition, holding or disposal of property, the enjoyment of educational
facilities, the holding of public office, or the carrying on of any occupation,
trade business or profession in (Subs. by the Central
Laws (Statute Reform) Ordinance, 1960 (21 of 1960), s. 3 and 2nd Sch. (with
effect from the 14th October, 1955), for "the provinces and the Capital of
the Federation" which had been subs. by A. O., 1949, for "British
India".)[Pakistan] by, and the franchise in (Subs. by the Central Laws (Statute Reform) Ordinance, 1960
(21 of 1960), s. 3 and 2nd Sch. (with effect from the 14th October, 1955), for
"the provinces and the Capital of the Federation" which had been
subs. by A. O., 1949, for "British India".)[Pakistan] of,
persons domiciled in British Possessions;
It is hereby enacted as follows:‑
1. Short title extent and
commencement-----‑‑(1) This Act may be called the Reciprocity
Act, 1943.
[(2) It extends to the whole of
Pakistan.]( Subs. by Ordinance 21 of 1960. s. 3 and 2nd
Sch. (with effect from the 14th October, 1955), for the original sub‑section
(2), as amended by A. O.,1949.)
[(3) It shall come into force on
the 1st day of September, 1943.]( Subs. by the
Reciprocity (Amdt.) Act., 1943 (22 of 1943), s. 3, for the original sub‑section
(3).)

Definition

THE RECIPROCITY ACT, 1943
THE RECIPROCITY
ACT, 1943
ACT No. IX or 1943
[31st March,
1943]
An Act to make
provisions on a basis of reciprocity in regard to
entry into,
travel, residence, the acquisition, holding or disposal
of property, the
enjoyment of educational facilities, the holding
of public office,
or the carrying on of any occupation, trade, business or profession in (Subs. by the Central Laws (Statute Reform) Ordinance, 1960
(21 of 1960), s. 3 and 2nd Sch. (with effect from the 14th October, 1955), for
"the provinces and the Capital of the Federation" which had been
subs. by A. O., 1949, for "British India".) [Pakistan] by,
and the franchise in (Subs. by the Central Laws
(Statute Reform) Ordinance, 1960 (21 of 1960), s. 3 and 2nd Sch. (with effect
from the 14th October, 1955), for "the provinces and the Capital of the
Federation" which had been subs. by A. O., 1949, for "British
India".)[Pakistan] of, persons domiciled in British Possessions.
WHEREAS it is expedient to make
provisions on a basis of reciprocity in regard to entry into, travel,
residence, the acquisition, holding or disposal of property, the enjoyment of
educational facilities, the holding of public office, or the carrying on of any
occupation, trade business or profession in (Subs. by
the Central Laws (Statute Reform) Ordinance, 1960 (21 of 1960), s. 3 and 2nd
Sch. (with effect from the 14th October, 1955), for "the provinces and the
Capital of the Federation" which had been subs. by A. O., 1949, for
"British India".)[Pakistan] by, and the franchise in (Subs. by the Central Laws (Statute Reform) Ordinance, 1960
(21 of 1960), s. 3 and 2nd Sch. (with effect from the 14th October, 1955), for
"the provinces and the Capital of the Federation" which had been
subs. by A. O., 1949, for "British India".)[Pakistan] of, persons
domiciled in British Possessions;
2. Definition----In this
Act, unless there is anything repugnant in the subject or context,‑
[(a) "British
possession" (Subs. ibid., for the original clause
(a).)means any part of His Majesty's dominions (The
words "exclusive of [Pakistan]" omitted by A. O., 1961, Art. 2 and
Sch. (with effect from the 23rd March, 1956). The word in crotchets was subs.
by A. O., 1949, for "British India".)* * *, and includes a
protectorate or' other territory administered by a British possession as a
mandatory on behalf of the League of Nations; and where parts of those
dominions are under both a central and a local legislature, the expression
shall mean either each part under a local legislature or all parts under the
central legislature.]
(b) "entry" includes landing at any port in (Subs. by the Central Laws (Statute Reform) Ordinance, 1960
(21 of 1960), s. 3 and 2nd Sch. (with effect from the 14th October, 1955), for
"the Provinces and the Capital of the Federation" which had been
subs. by A. O., 1949, for "British India".)[Pakistan] during
the stay in (Subs. by the Central Laws (Statute Reform)
Ordinance, 1960 (21 of 1960), s. 3 and 2nd Sch. (with effect from the 14th
October, 1955), for "the Provinces and the Capital of the Federation"
which had been subs. by A. O., 1949, for "British India".)[Pakistan]
of a ship or aircraft on its way to a destination outside (Subs. by the Central Laws (Statute Reform) Ordinance, 1960
(21 of 1960), s. 3 and 2nd Sch. (with effect from the 14th October, 1955), for
"the Provinces and the Capital of the Federation" which had been
subs. by A. O., 1949, for "British India".)[Pakistan].

Power of Central Government to impose reciprocal disabilities on persons domiciled in British possessions

provisions on a basis of reciprocity in regard to
entry into,

of property, the

or the carrying on of any occupation, trade, business or profession in (Subs. by the Central Laws (Statute Reform) Ordinance, 1960
(21 of 1960), s. 3 and 2nd Sch. (with effect from the 14th October, 1955), for
"the provinces and the Capital of the Federation" which had been
subs. by A. O., 1949, for "British India".) [Pakistan] by,

Federation" which had been subs. by A. O., 1949, for "British
India".)[Pakistan] of, persons domiciled in British Possessions.
WHEREAS it is expedient to make
provisions on a basis of reciprocity in regard to entry into, travel,
residence, the acquisition, holding or disposal of property, the enjoyment of
educational facilities, the holding of public office, or the carrying on of any
occupation, trade business or profession in (Subs. by
the Central Laws (Statute Reform) Ordinance, 1960 (21 of 1960), s. 3 and 2nd
Sch. (with effect from the 14th October, 1955), for "the provinces and the
Capital of the Federation" which had been subs. by A. O., 1949, for
"British India".)[Pakistan] by, and the franchise in (Subs. by the Central Laws (Statute Reform) Ordinance, 1960
(21 of 1960), s. 3 and 2nd Sch. (with effect from the 14th October, 1955), for
"the provinces and the Capital of the Federation" which had been
subs. by A. O., 1949, for "British India".)[Pakistan] of, persons
domiciled in British Possessions;
[3. Power of Central
Government to impose reciprocal disabilities on persons domiciled in British
possessions------( Subs. by the Reciprocity (Amdt.)
Act, 1943 (22 of 1943), for the original section 3.)Where by the
law or practice of any British possession persons of (Subs.
by A. O., 1949, for "Indian origin".)[Indo‑Pakistan
origin] are subject in that British possession to disabilities in respect of
entry into, or travel, resi dence, the acquisition, holding or disposal of
property, the enjoy ment of educational facilities, the holding of public
office, the carrying on of any occupation, trade, business or profession, or
the exercise of the franchise in, that British possession, to which in respect
of the like matters in (Subs. by the Central Laws
(Statute Reform) Ordinance, 1960 (21 of 1960), s. 3 and 2nd Sch. (with effect
from the 14th October, 1955), for "the Provinces and the Capital of the
Federation" which had been subs. by A. O., 1949, for "British India".)[Pakistan]
persons domiciled in that British possession are not subject in (Subs. by the Central Laws (Statute Reform) Ordinance, 1960
(21 of 1960), s. 3 and 2nd Sch. (with effect from the 14th October, 1955), for
"the Provinces and the Capital of the Federation" which had been
subs. by A. O., 1949, for "British India".)[Pakistan], the Cen tral
Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, direct that the same
disabilities or disabilities as similar thereto as may be shall,
notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in
force, be imposed in (Subs. by the Central Laws
(Statute Reform) Ordinance, 1960 (21 of 1960), s. 3 and 2nd Sch. (with effect
from the 14th October, 1955), for "the Provinces and the Capital of the
Federation" which had been subs. by A. O., 1949, for "British
India".)[Pakistan] on persons not being of (Subs. by A. O., 1949, for "Indian origin".)[Indo‑Pakistan
origin] who are domiciled in that British possession.]

entry into,

of property, the

of public office,
or the carrying on of any occupation, trade, business or profession in (Subs. by the Central Laws (Statute Reform) Ordinance, 1960
(21 of 1960), s. 3 and 2nd Sch. (with effect from the 14th October, 1955), for
"the provinces and the Capital of the Federation" which had been
subs. by A. O., 1949, for "British India".) [Pakistan] by,

provisions on a basis of reciprocity in regard to entry into, travel,
residence, the acquisition, holding or disposal of property, the enjoyment of
educational facilities, the holding of public office, or the carrying on of any
occupation, trade business or profession in (Subs. by
the Central Laws (Statute Reform) Ordinance, 1960 (21 of 1960), s. 3 and 2nd
Sch. (with effect from the 14th October, 1955), for "the provinces and the
Capital of the Federation" which had been subs. by A. O., 1949, for
"British India".)[Pakistan] by, and the franchise in (Subs. by the Central Laws (Statute Reform) Ordinance, 1960
(21 of 1960), s. 3 and 2nd Sch. (with effect from the 14th October, 1955), for
"the provinces and the Capital of the Federation" which had been
subs. by A. O., 1949, for "British India".)[Pakistan] of, persons
domiciled in British Possessions;
4. Burden of proof on person
claiming exemption-----If any person alleged to be domiciled in any British
Posses sion and to be subject to the provisions of this Act pleads that he is
not so domiciled, or that the provisions of this Act do not apply to him, the
onus of proving the truth of such a plea shall be on him.

hostilities, apply to any person domi ciled in that British possession who is a
member of its armed forces.]

Power to make rules

THE RECIPROCITY ACT, 1943
THE RECIPROCITY
ACT, 1943
ACT No. IX or 1943
[31st March,
1943]
An Act to make
provisions on a basis of reciprocity in regard to
entry into,
travel, residence, the acquisition, holding or disposal
of property, the
enjoyment of educational facilities, the holding
of public office,
or the carrying on of any occupation, trade, business or profession in (Subs. by the Central Laws (Statute Reform) Ordinance, 1960
(21 of 1960), s. 3 and 2nd Sch. (with effect from the 14th October, 1955), for
"the provinces and the Capital of the Federation" which had been
subs. by A. O., 1949, for "British India".) [Pakistan] by,
and the franchise in (Subs. by the Central Laws
(Statute Reform) Ordinance, 1960 (21 of 1960), s. 3 and 2nd Sch. (with effect
from the 14th October, 1955), for "the provinces and the Capital of the
Federation" which had been subs. by A. O., 1949, for "British
India".)[Pakistan] of, persons domiciled in British Possessions.
WHEREAS it is expedient to make
provisions on a basis of reciprocity in regard to entry into, travel,
residence, the acquisition, holding or disposal of property, the enjoyment of
educational facilities, the holding of public office, or the carrying on of any
occupation, trade business or profession in (Subs. by
the Central Laws (Statute Reform) Ordinance, 1960 (21 of 1960), s. 3 and 2nd
Sch. (with effect from the 14th October, 1955), for "the provinces and the
Capital of the Federation" which had been subs. by A. O., 1949, for
"British India".)[Pakistan] by, and the franchise in (Subs. by the Central Laws (Statute Reform) Ordinance, 1960
(21 of 1960), s. 3 and 2nd Sch. (with effect from the 14th October, 1955), for
"the provinces and the Capital of the Federation" which had been
subs. by A. O., 1949, for "British India".)[Pakistan] of, persons
domiciled in British Possessions;
[6. Power to make rules----‑(
Subs. by the Reciprocity (Amdt.) Act, 1943 (22 of 1943), s. 5, for the original
section 6.)(1) The‑Central Government may, by notification in the
official Gazette, make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Act.
(2) In particular and without
prejudice to the generality of the foregoing power, rules made under this
section may provide‑
(a) for the setting up of
machinery to ascertain the disabili ties in respect of any of the matters
specified in section 3 to which persons of (Subs. by A.
O., 1949, for "Indian origin".)[Indo‑Pakistan origin]
are subject in any British possession;
(b) for the establishment of a
suitable agency to administer the rules and for defining its functions and
powers;
(c) for specifying the
disabilities that shall, when a direction has been made under section 3, be
imposed in (Subs. by the Central Laws (Stature Reform)
Ordinance, 1960 (21 of 1960), s. 3 and 2nd Sch. (with effect from the 14th
October, 1955), for "the Provinces and the Capital of the Federation"
which had been subs. by A. O., 1949, for "British India".)[Pakis tan]
on persons not being of (Subs. by A. O., 1949, for
"Indian origin".)[Indo‑Pakistan origin] who are
domiciled in any British possession and for the imposition on them of the
disabilities so specified;
(d) for the enforcement, by the
prescription of a penalty by way of imprisonment or fine or both, of any rule
made under clause (c);
(e) for authorising the arrest of
any person contravening or reasonably suspected of contravening any rule made
under clause (c), and for prescribing the duties of public servants and others
in regard to such arrests.]
